blocks.text: Mastering Slack for b2b sales reps on mac

Sales reps often feel buried under a mountain of notifications. You need a clean workspace to stay focused on your quota. Use the built-in Slack search modifiers to find information quickly. Press Command + K to open the quick switcher. This lets you jump to any conversation in seconds. You no longer have to scroll through long lists to find a specific channel or person.

items: Use Command + / to open the cheat sheet for all keyboard shortcuts.
Use Command + F to search within the current channel.
Use Shift + Enter to add a line break instead of sending your message early.
Use Command + B and Command + I for quick text formatting.

blocks.text: Administrative work takes up a large portion of your day. You can reduce this by setting up clear communication habits. Use threads for all feedback on deal documents. This keeps the main channel clean and prevents important details from getting lost. If you need to follow up on a specific message later, use the save feature. Press the three dots menu on any message and click Save for later.

Constant pings break your flow state. Go to Preferences by pressing Command + , on your Mac. Under the Notifications tab, set your schedule to match your work hours. You can also use the /dnd command to pause notifications for a specific amount of time. This is helpful when you are preparing for a demo or writing a complex proposal.
Mute channels that are not relevant to your current deals. Right-click the channel name in the sidebar and select Mute channel. This hides the channel from your unread counts.
blocks.title: Quiet your sidebar

blocks.text: Lazur helps you find your way around the Slack interface. If you are stuck, hold Option + Command and ask where a specific setting is. Lazur will draw a circle around the menu item. This is much faster than digging through submenus. You can also ask Lazur to explain how to perform a task. It will guide you through the process step by step.

Sales is a team sport. Use Slack huddles for quick syncs with your sales engineer or manager. You can share your screen instantly by clicking the monitor icon in the huddle window. This prevents long email chains about technical questions. Keep your deal status updated by using a dedicated channel for each account. Use the pin feature to keep the most important documents at the top of the channel.
Advanced search techniques for sales reps

Searching is a core skill for any rep. Use modifiers to narrow down your results. Type from:@name to see messages from a specific person. Use in:#channel to limit your search to a specific project. You can also use has:link or has:file to find documents you shared with a prospect. This saves time when you need to find a contract from three months ago.

Your team needs to know when you are busy. Use the status feature to set your current activity. Click your profile picture and select Update status. You can set a status like In a demo or Prospecting. This manages expectations and reduces interruptions. You can also set a duration for your status so it automatically clears when you are finished.

Sometimes the app might slow down or act up. If you notice performance issues, clear your cache. Go to Help > Troubleshooting > Clear Cache and Restart. This often fixes minor bugs without needing to reinstall the app. Ensure you are running the latest version of macOS for the best experience. Slack requires macOS 14 or above for the most recent features.

faq.question: Can I use Slack shortcuts on Mac?
faq.answer: Yes, Slack supports many keyboard shortcuts on Mac. Press Command + / to see the full list of available commands.

faq.question: How do I find a message I sent earlier?
faq.answer: Use the search bar at the top of Slack. You can use the from:me modifier to filter results to messages you have sent.

faq.question: What should I do if Slack is running slowly?
faq.answer: Try clearing your cache by going to Help > Troubleshooting > Clear Cache and Restart in the Slack desktop app.

faq.question: How can I keep my deal channels organized?
faq.answer: Use threads for all discussions related to a specific message. This keeps the main channel feed clean and easy to read.
